walkthroughs.body_html: Average retreat 1.8 m/yr; locally 4-10 m/yr in storm years. Since Roman times 29 villages lost: Wilsthorpe (medieval), Auburn, Hyde, Owthorne. Domesday Book (1086) lists settlements now offshore. Total coastline retreat ~4 km in 2000 years.

£2 million spent on two rock groynes plus rip-rap revetment. Successfully halted erosion at Mappleton but caused 1.8 m/yr increased erosion at Cowden (3 km south). Cost-benefit calculation excluded downdrift impacts; case used to argue for ICZM.

Most of Holderness designated 'no active intervention': economic value of farmland too low to justify defences. Settlements like Hornsea and Withernsea defended. Spurn Head 'managed realignment' after 2013 breach. Property owners face uninsured loss.

El Nino is the name of a specific hurricane that hit Mexico.

mcqs.q: Why do some rivers form deltas and others form estuaries?
options: Plates move because of ocean tides pulling on the crust.
Deltas form in cold climates and estuaries in warm climates.
Deltas form on big rivers and estuaries on small ones.
Deltas form where rivers deposit sediment faster than the sea can remove it (calm seas, heavy load); estuaries form where tidal energy removes sediment (strong tides).
